content: Neomycin sulfate, polymyxin B sulfate, and gramicidin are components of an antiseptic solution that is approved by the FDA for the treatment of superficial infections of the external eye and its associated structures caused by susceptible bacteria. These infections include conditions such as conjunctivitis, keratitis, keratoconjunctivitis, blepharitis, and blepharoconjunctivitis. The solution is applied topically, with a recommended dosage of one to two drops in the affected eye every four hours for a duration of 7 to 10 days. In severe cases, the dosage may be increased to two drops every hour. The solution is contraindicated in individuals who have demonstrated hypersensitivity to any of its components. It is important to note that this medication is not intended for injection into the eye, including the anterior chamber or subconjunctival space. Topical antibiotics, particularly neomycin sulfate, may cause cutaneous sensitization, which can manifest as itching, redness, or swelling of the conjunctiva and eyelid. In some cases, sensitization may present as a failure to heal. Patients should discontinue use if these symptoms occur, and the symptoms typically resolve after stopping the medication. Adverse reactions associated with this solution include allergic sensitization reactions such as itching, swelling, and conjunctival erythema. Rarely, more severe hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported. Local irritation upon instillation has also been noted. The mechanism of action of this combination therapy involves the antibacterial properties of its components. Neomycin is an aminoglycoside antibiotic that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to ribosomal RNA, leading to misreading of the bacterial genetic code. Polymyxin B disrupts the bacterial cell membrane by interacting with its phospholipid components, increasing membrane permeability. Gramicidin forms channels in the bacterial cell membrane, allowing inorganic cations to pass through, which disrupts the membrane's integrity. Together, these agents are effective against a range of microorganisms, including Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Escherichia coli, Haemophilus influenzae, Klebsiella/Enterobacter species, Neisseria species, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. However, the solution does not provide adequate coverage against Serratia marcescens. The solution is supplied in a sterile 10 mL plastic dispenser bottle and should be stored at a temperature of 15° to 25°C (59° to 77°F), protected from light. It contains inactive ingredients such as alcohol, thimerosal (as a preservative), propylene glycol, sodium chloride, and water for injection. There is limited information regarding the use of this medication in specific populations, including pregnant or nursing women, pediatric patients, elderly patients, and individuals with renal or hepatic impairment. It is classified as Pregnancy Category C, meaning that animal reproduction studies have not been conducted, and its effects on fetal harm or reproductive capacity are unknown. Caution is advised when administering this medication to nursing mothers, as it is not known whether the drug is excreted in human milk. Patients should be informed about the proper use of this medication and advised to discontinue use if signs of hypersensitivity or adverse reactions occur. Additionally, there is no established interaction between this medication and alcohol, but patients should consult their healthcare provider regarding alcohol consumption while using this product.
